gary_2026_11_06_app_after_dark_mobile_ap.title: App After Dark: Mobile App Hackathon
gary_2026_11_06_app_after_dark_mobile_ap.label: Tech / AI
gary_2026_11_06_app_after_dark_mobile_ap.summary: Gary's Guide: What's happening? Bilt.me is teaming up with The AI Collective, Veris.ai & Mobbin to host Mobile App Hackathon Night in New York: an evening for getting a real mobile app out of your head & onto your phone, with AI. A friendly hackathon where the only rule is to ship something by the end of the night. Most app ideas never leave the Notes app. Tonight yours does. No code needed. Bring a fresh idea or something you've already started. Describe what you want in plain language, keep refining it, & leave with an app running on your phone that you can show people. All you need is a laptop & the willingness to call something done. You'll be hacking alongside founders, designers, coders & people with too many ideas in their Notes app. Come solo or bring a friend, & we'll help you find teammates. Why come? Build your app with Bilt.me & meet the people building with AI in New York. Plus a Mobbin discount for everyone who comes. Pizza on us Format Teams of one or two. A quick kickoff, then three hours of heads-down hacking with a clear finish line: get it working on your phone. We wrap with demos, so everyone sees what got shipped. What to expect A short intro to building with Bilt.me Time to hack, test on your phone & ask questions Friendly feedback from the room Demos at the end Good conversations & new people to build with Who is it for? Anyone who wants to stop thinking about an app & start shipping one: aspiring founders, designers, creatives, AI-curious builders, & people who have never written code. What to bring? A laptop Your phone An idea, or the app you've already started Co-hosted with The AI Collective The AI Collective is a global non-profit building the human layer for the AI era. We unite 200,000+ leaders, builders, & stakeholders across 100+ forums worldwide to democratize the frontier, build trust, & coordinate how society navigates the rapid acceleration of technological progress. Our partners Veris.ai is supporting the night as a partner. Veris AI builds simulated environments where companies train & test AI agents before putting them into real use. Think of it as a practice arena that lets enterprise AI agents make mistakes safely before they touch real customers or systems. Mobbin is the design reference library behind a lot of the apps you love: real screens & flows from the best apps out there, all in one place. Tonight it's your shortcut to great design. Find a screen you love on Mobbin, screenshot it, & drop it into Bilt as the starting point for your app. Everyone who comes gets a Mobbin discount code on the night. Seats are limited & we read every application. About Bilt.me Bilt turns a plain-language idea into a real native mobile app, with the frontend, database & login all built for you, ready to test on your phone & publish to the App Store & Google Play. When: Friday 6th November 2026 Time: 6pm to 9pm Where: New York, venue to be announced. We'll share the location with approved guests. Entry: Free Bilt.me credits: included, sponsored Hosted by Bilt.me in collaboration with The AI Collective (aicollective.com), Veris.ai & Mobbin (mobbin.com) We take pictures during this event & will use those pictures for marketing. If you don't wish to be photographed, let us know in advance & we can accommodate. Link to Bilt privacy policy: bilt.me/privacy

gary_2026_11_10_gild_ai_forum_ai_engg_le.summary: Gary's Guide: This GILD AI Forum brings together CTOs, VPs of Engineering, Heads of AI, & senior technical leaders for candid conversations about building, scaling, & implementing AI inside their companies. This isn't a conference. It's not a panel. It's a small, curated room of technical leaders sharing what's actually working, what's not, & the real challenges of shipping AI in the AI era. Each Forum opens with a Conversation Starter, a practitioner sharing what their team is building with AI, followed by open Q&A. From there, the room breaks into intimate discussions where everyone has a seat at the table. Every attendee brings their own experience. Every attendee contributes. No pitches. No performative networking. Just senior technical leaders being honest about the architectures they're choosing, the tradeoffs they're making, & what they wish they'd figured out sooner. TRENDING THEMES FOR THIS SESSION Conversations at the Forum are shaped by what technical leaders bring to the table. Themes likely to surface this evening include: From AI pilots to AI in production: breaking out of the proof-of-concept trap & scaling agents into real workflows Connecting AI to legacy systems: architectural patterns for integrating modern AI with 20-year-old stacks without breaking everything The AI tooling budget problem: balancing experimentation with unsustainable spend as engineers blow through AI tool budgets Engineers as curators, not creators: the shift from writing code to orchestrating AI agents, reusable components, & external services MCP, multi-agent systems, & the orchestration layer: what's working, what's overhyped, & what technical leaders are actually building Guardrails & governance for AI-generated code: who's accountable when the AI writes it, & what review processes actually hold up in production Presented in partnership with Tecla Tecla gives companies flexible access to vetted talent across the US & Latin America, developed for AI-native work & available from fractional engagements to dedicated nearshore pods. Learn more at www.tecla.io THE FORMAT Intentionally small & highly curated, 20 to 25 max. A seated round-table dinner, private & off the record under Chatham House Rules. AGENDA 6:00 - 6:30 PM Cocktails & passed appetizers 6:30 - 7:00 PM Dinner is served Find a seat & get comfortable. 6:45 - 6:50 PM GILD & Partner Welcome A few words from the GILD team & our partners on what the night holds & how we'll spend it together. 6:50 - 7:00 PM Conversation Starter A fellow engineering leader opens the discussion with a candid perspective on AI, with a brief Q&A. 7:00 - 8:00 PM Table discussions 8:00 - 8:30 PM Open mingling WHO THIS IS FOR Founders CEOs CTOs VPs of Engineering Heads of AI Technical Leaders Product Leaders This session is for leaders responsible for building, deploying, & maintaining AI systems in production. Chatham House Rules apply. Discussion stays private.

gary_2026_11_11_startup_pitch_5_founders.title: Startup Pitch - 5 Founders On Stage
gary_2026_11_11_startup_pitch_5_founders.label: Startup / Business
gary_2026_11_11_startup_pitch_5_founders.summary: Gary's Guide: You've been running the idea past AI. AI has never once told you it wouldn't work. Tonight you get a room that will. Five founders, five minutes each, American Whiskey - Midtown in New York. Wednesday. Three reasons people come back: You get a table, not a lap of the room. You pick a topic the room voted on & stay there for the hour, instead of wandering with a drink looking for a gap in somebody else's conversation. You get a stage short enough to be honest. Five minutes each, no slides read out loud, then the room asks questions. The questions are the good part. You get the hour after. The stage ends, nobody's performing any more, & the floor stays open. That's the hour people actually remember. Your ticket is also a login: Most events end when you walk out. This one hands you a link: your profile, who else is coming before you get there, a group chat for this specific Wednesday, & a recap afterwards of who you actually met. Then you land in the New York space & stay there. That's where the second conversation happens, the one you meant to have before the room got loud. Free with your ticket, on the web or in Telegram: ascentvalley.com/community Is this your room? Yes, if you're building something, anywhere from the first line of code to Series A. Or you run a function at a company that's scaling, write the code, do the hiring, or you're still deciding whether to start. Probably not, if what you're picturing is a room full of investors. How that actually works is further down, & it's better than the picture. Want the stage? Apply at Five founders an evening, & we answer everybody, including the people we don't pick. Applying is free, but you do need a ticket, because we check the order number. Never pitched before? Five minutes is short enough that it's over before the nerves have finished arriving. What we don't promise, & what we do instead We don't promise an investor will be in the room on any given Wednesday. Angels & people who work at funds come, some Wednesdays several of them, & we won't tell you in advance who's coming, because we don't know. We don't run a judging panel, hand out a prize, or keep a leaderboard. Here's what doesn't depend on who walks in that night. Your application to the stage becomes your profile in our startup directory, & a person reads it, not a scoring script. Once you're verified, that profile sits in front of the funds & angels in our network, & they ask for the introduction themselves when your company matches what they're actually looking for. You choose whether you're in the weekly digest & you can leave it any time. We never sell your details, we don't take equity, we don't take a cut of your round, & we don't give investment advice. Which means the room on Wednesday isn't the whole opportunity. It's the part you can see: ascentvalley.com/pitch Why it's worth a Wednesday Watching somebody explain their company in five minutes teaches you more about explaining yours than another evening alone with the deck. You'll hear the question you've been quietly avoiding get asked out loud to somebody else, & you get to watch how they handle it. That skill travels. It works on a first date, in a performance review, & at the dinner where somebody asks what you do & you've got twenty seconds before their eyes move on. So bring the friend who keeps saying they have an idea. Five minutes on that stage is the shortest distance between having an idea & finding out what a room full of strangers thinks of it.
